_about: Layer 2 (product line), layer 3 (family: none — Cisco names no family over its optics series) and layer 4 (series) of Cisco pluggable optics and cables, 14 Sep 2026 (layers round 3, transceiver + interfaces-modules). The stored series labels name the HOST platform ('Catalyst 6500', 'MDS 9500', 'Transceiver Modules') and say nothing about the optic, so every series is decided by the SKU's form-factor and speed family, in Cisco's own transceiver taxonomy. Order is load-bearing: same-cage direct-attach / active optical cables first (SFP-10G-AOC is a cable, not an SFP+) — a BREAKOUT cable is refused there and goes to its host cage's speed series (operator, round 3) — then Meraki, cable-access, Fibre Channel, ONS/NCS 2000, coherent, DWDM, CWDM, SONET, then Ethernet from the highest speed down. Round 3 fixed the four SKU rules the switches + routers review recorded as too broad (ACU took UK power cords, GBIC Catalyst 6500 line cards, DWDM router line cards, 800G an ISR 880 PoE module). No role axis.

series.series: DAC and AOC cables (SFP+ / SFP28 / SFP56 / QSFP / QSFP-DD)
series.note: same-cage cables only. A breakout (one QSFP / QSFP-DD host cage fanned out to 2 or 4 smaller cages: QSFP-4SFP25G-CU1M, QSFP-4X10G-AOC1M, QDD-4ZQ100-CU1M) is refused by the lookahead and placed in its host cage's speed series with kind breakout-cable (operator, layers round 3); the standing check asserts no breakout-cable row sits here. (?<!E)CU (layers round 3, optical round): the copper-DAC rule claimed the External Connection Units 15454-M6-ECU2, NCS2006-ECU60-S= and NCS4K-ECU2 in optical-networking
^MA- fenced to the optics and cables it names (layers round 3, wireless round): the bare rule claimed wireless' Meraki MR antennas, mounts and power adapters (MA-ANT-3-A1 …, 30 rows)

lines.no_family_reason: three optic families sold with three different platforms (Remote PHY devices and shelves, Prisma II / RF Gateway, Catalyst PON and ME 4600 OLTs); Cisco names no family over them

series.note: decided home (operator, layers round 3): the 120 RPHY-S10G-<reach>-<channel>= rows are transceivers — Cisco's own bulletin calls them 'Remote PHY SFPs'; the Remote PHY shelves, RPDs and cabling stay in video. The 57 video rows carry move plans in (run after the re-audit); video's ^RPHY rule is recorded as too broad and fenced in the video round

series.series: GPON / XGS-PON OLT and RF Gateway SFPs
series.note: SFP-10G-OLT20-X (an XGS-PON OLT SFP+) was in 10G SFP+ by its speed prefix; a PON OLT optic is sold with the PON line (layers round 3)

series.series: MDS Fibre Channel SFP / X2 / CWDM
series.note: ^DS-FC-SW places DS-FC-SW-4PK= (a 4-pack of FC SFPs) planned in from storage-networking. The DS-CWDM rule refuses the MDS CWDM passives (DS-CWDM-MUX8A=, DS-CWDMOADM4A=, DS-CWDMCHASSIS=), which are planned to optical-networking and must not fall back to an optic series if a plan is withdrawn (reviewer A-11, layers round 3)

the ONS rule names the optic and cable-assembly tokens opticalKind names, not every ONS- SKU: the bare prefix claimed the patch cord ONS-CAB-CS-LC-5= in interfaces-modules (reviewer A-11, layers round 3). The twelve 15454-SFP / 15454E-SFP rows are planned to optical-networking (operator: ^15454 goes with the ONS 15454 platform, and the asymmetry with the ONS-prefixed optics that stay here is intended); the 15216-GBIC rows sit in GBIC (legacy)

QSFP100GMX1/MX2-2/-20-BUN are Routed Optical Networking bundles of the DP01QS28-MX1/MX2 100G DCO QSFP28 (were in 100G QSFP28 by prefix); Q100-ZR4-S-EA= is a fixed 80 km 100GBASE-ZR4 QSFP28, not coherent, and moved to 100G QSFP28 (layers round 3)

series.series: DWDM SFP / SFP+ / XFP / X2 / XENPAK
series.note: the unanchored DWDM token took CRS / ASR 9000 / NCS 5500 DWDM line cards in routers (review record: fix in the transceiver round) and is gone; the one transceiver row it named, X2-10G-DWDM, is a family placeholder with a class plan (operator, layers round 3). DWDM-GBIC rows sit in GBIC (legacy)
CWDM-GBIC rows sit in GBIC (legacy); the CWDM-OADM1 / OADM4 plug-ins are planned to optical-networking with the CWDM-MUX rows (layers round 3)

series.series: OC-3 / OC-12 / OC-48 and T1/E1/T3 SFPs

lines.no_family_reason: Cisco sells Ethernet optics by form factor and speed (SFP, SFP+, SFP28, SFP56, QSFP+, QSFP28, QSFP-DD, OSFP, CFP / CPAK, X2 / XENPAK / XFP, GBIC); each series is that form-factor family and Cisco names no family grouping them

series.note: QDD-2X400G-FR4 and QDD-8X100G-FR are QSFP-DD800 modules by their own names (were in 200G / 400G by the QDD prefix); the bare 800G token took the ISR 880 PoE module 800G2-POE-2 (review record) and is gone (layers round 3)

QSFP-4S50-CU1M / 2M / 3M (a 200G QSFP56 host fanned out to 4 x 50G SFP56) sit here by their host cage like every other breakout (reviewer A-2, layers round 3; they were in 50G SFP56 by the fan-out end)
QSFP-40/100-SRBD (dual-rate 40/100G BiDi QSFP28) was in 40G QSFP+: the rule named only the QSFP-40/100G spelling (layers round 3)

was '100G CFP / CFP2 / CPAK / CXP'; the series also holds the CFP-40G modules and the CPAK 10x10G. ^NCS-FAB-OPT (layers round 3, pre-ruling C4): NCS-FAB-OPT(=) "Bundle of 96 CXP-100G-SR12", planned in from interfaces-modules — kind pluggable at the unit, pack quantity 96 parked with the other packs (decision 6)
CSP-SFP-1WSR / 1WLR are 10GE SFP+ for the CSP 2100's Intel NICs (were in 1G by prefix); EXP-10GSFP places the Expressway SFP+ planned in from unified-communications (layers round 3)

every GBIC form-factor optic outside a platform line: the 1000BASE GBICs WS-G548x and the WDM GBICs DWDM-GBIC (32), CWDM-GBIC (8) and 15216-GBIC (2) (operator, layers round 3). The bare GBIC token took Catalyst 6500 GBIC line cards (review record) and is gone. ONS-GC-GE-* GBICs stay with the ONS / NCS 2000 platform line

series.series: CVR converter modules, trays and brackets
